metaDescription: Six 10 ft portable wheelchair ramps compared on width, listed capacity, handrails, folding style and the rise each page says it suits.
introParagraphs: A 10 ft portable ramp is the length people reach for when a step or a porch edge is too tall for a short threshold ramp. The length is only half the story, because a ramp is judged by the rise it climbs. A common rule of thumb is one inch of rise for every twelve inches of run, which makes a 10 ft ramp comfortable for roughly a 10 in rise, and noticeably steeper for anything taller. Every listing in this lineup states a rise range, and those ranges deserve a careful read.

We compared six models: the CAMMOO ramp with handrails, the NUWJBYE with full-length handrails, the VEVOR, a second CAMMOO folding ramp, the LEMNISCATE with mid-span legs and the HOMCOM. The comparison covers stated capacity, width, rails and edge barriers, surface, folding format and the step height each page names. Where a listing leaves out a number, we say so.

A portable ramp is not a code-compliant permanent ramp, and the right slope depends on the user, the chair or scooter and who is helping. Check the mobility device owner guide for incline limits and ask an occupational therapist before relying on any ramp, especially at the steep end of a listed range.

products.name: CAMMOO 10 FT Wheelchair Ramp with Handrails, 1200 lb
products.description:
CAMMOO builds this model at 131.05 in long, 36 in wide and 34 in high at the handrails, with adjustable legs and a listed 1200 lb capacity. The page says it fits steps from 10 to 30 in with a ramp-to-ground angle of 7 to 14 degrees, and it quotes the ADA formula of step height times twelve for ramp length. The handrail grips are soft, and minor creases from packaging are noted as normal.

Handrails and a wider deck make a real difference on a ramp that someone has to climb or be pushed along. They give a place to steady the hand and a barrier at the edge. The listing is also unusually frank about angle, which shows how steep the top of its range is.

A 10 ft length with a 30 in rise is much steeper than the twelve-to-one rule of thumb, so treat the upper range as a limit to check, not a recommendation. At 36 in wide it matches the NUWJBYE, and it is wider than the 29.1 in CAMMOO folding ramp. It is the most fully equipped option here.
products.bestFor: Regular home use where handrails, width and a high rating matter.
pros: Lists 1200 lb capacity, the highest here
36 in deck with 34 in tall handrails
Adjustable legs to match the step height
States the ramp-to-ground angle range
cons: Steep at the top of its 10 to 30 in range
Heavier and bulkier than a bare folding ramp

products.name: NUWJBYE 10 FT Wheelchair Ramp with Handrails, 850 lb
products.description:
NUWJBYE lists a 10 ft by 36 in deck with an 850 lb capacity and dual integrated handrails that run the full length of both sides. The page says the metal surface is high-traction for rain or snow, and reflective strips help visibility at night. The extra width is promoted for wheelchairs, scooters and walkers.

Full-length rails are the headline. On a long incline, a hand-hold for the user and the helper makes the ramp easier to use, and the rails also act as edge barriers. A 36 in deck gives more clearance for hands and wheels than the 29 in decks common on folding ramps.

The page does not give a step height range in the details we reviewed, so you must confirm the rise you can handle with the seller. Compared with the CAMMOO 1200 lb handrail model, it lists a lower rating. Against the bare VEVOR, it adds rails and width.
products.bestFor: Users who want rails on both sides and a wide, flat deck.
pros: Dual handrails run the full ramp length
36 in width gives extra clearance
Reflective strips help visibility at night
850 lb capacity stated in the listing
cons: No step height range in the details reviewed
Rails and width add weight and bulk

products.name: VEVOR 10FT Portable Wheelchair Ramp, 800 lb
products.description:
VEVOR states a 10 to 20 in rise range for this 10 ft ramp, which is a tighter and more conservative window than the 10 to 30 in on several rivals. It supports 800 lb, with a grooved aluminum surface, a full-coverage non-slip coating, raised side baffles and high-visibility reflective strips. The page describes use at doors, garages and driveway curbs.

The narrower range is a quiet strength. A 20 in rise over 120 in is a one-to-six slope, still steep, but less extreme than a 30 in climb, and the maker is open about where it stops. Raised baffles and reflective strips handle edges and low light.

It has no handrails, unlike the CAMMOO and NUWJBYE, so the user relies on the chair or a helper. The folding style carries over from other 10 ft ramps. Choose it if your rise sits comfortably in the lower half of the typical range.
products.bestFor: Rises between 10 and 20 in where a plain folding ramp is enough.
pros: States a 10 to 20 in rise range
800 lb capacity listed for wheelchairs and scooters
Grooved surface plus non-slip coating
Raised baffles and reflective strips
cons: No handrails, so balance relies on the chair or a helper
Narrower rise range than some rivals

products.name: CAMMOO 10 FT Aluminum Wheelchair Ramp, 800 lb
products.description:
CAMMOO makes a folding 10 ft ramp from high-strength aluminum alloy, 120 in long, 29.1 in wide and 1.77 in thick when unfolded, with an 800 lb heavy-duty capacity. The page offers two folding options, a two-fold and another format, so you can choose the carry size. Three anti-slip protections are advertised for home wheelchairs and mobility aids.

The compact folded shape is the selling point. Folding in two puts the ramp in a closet or trunk, and the alternate fold changes the footprint. A 29.1 in deck is typical of folding ramps and narrower than the 36 in rails models.

The listing in the details we reviewed does not give a step height range, so check it before ordering. Against the VEVOR it lists the same 800 lb, and against the CAMMOO handrail model it trades width and rails for storage. It suits someone who stows the ramp between uses.
products.bestFor: Households that store the ramp between uses and want fold choices.
pros: Two folding options for different storage
800 lb heavy-duty capacity listed
Thin 1.77 in profile when unfolded
Three anti-slip protections advertised
cons: No step height range in the details reviewed
29.1 in deck is narrower than rail models

products.name: LEMNISCATE 10FT Portable Wheelchair Ramp with Handle
products.description:
LEMNISCATE adds adjustable mid-span stabilizing legs to a folding 10 ft ramp, intended to stop bowing under load and reduce wobble. The unfolded size is 120 by 29 by 2 in, the page says it suits steps of 10 to 30 in, and side baffles and transition plates are included. A carry handle and folding design help with moving it.

Center support is the useful idea. A long aluminum span can flex in the middle, and a leg under it gives the deck something to rest on. Legs add a step to setup, so check they are set and locked each time.

The details we reviewed do not state a weight capacity, which is a notable gap next to the 800 lb on the VEVOR and CAMMOO. Treat the top of its step range with the same caution as the other 10 to 30 in ramps. It is for those who want a flatter, steadier deck.
products.bestFor: Heavier use where a flex-free middle matters, once capacity is confirmed.
pros: Adjustable mid-span legs support the center
Side baffles and transition plates included
Carry handle helps with moving it
States a 10 to 30 in step window
cons: Weight capacity not given in the details
Extra legs add a setup step each time

products.name: HOMCOM 10FT Aluminum Wheelchair Ramp, 594 lb
products.description:
HOMCOM sells a 10 ft aluminum ramp with a listed 594 lb capacity, made from anti-corrosive alloy and covered with a black frosted skidproof carpet. Two high side walls help prevent a wheel from leaving the edge. The page markets it for wheelchairs, scooters, bikes and other awkward loads.

The carpeted surface is different from the grooved metal of the VEVOR. It can feel grippy and quiet, but carpet holds water and grit, so it needs drying and brushing. The multipurpose pitch is broader than most, and the page calls it a threshold ramp, which can blur the use.

Its capacity is the lowest in this lineup, below the 800 lb of the VEVOR and CAMMOO 800 and well below the CAMMOO 1200. The page gives no step range in the details reviewed. It fits lighter loads and occasional use, provided the user and device weights are comfortably under the rating.
products.bestFor: Lighter occasional loads with a quiet, grippy surface.

Page also names scooters and bikes as uses

No step height range in the details

buyingCriteria.criterion: Rise and the slope it creates
buyingCriteria.explanation: Measure the vertical height from the ground to the top of the step, including any threshold. A 10 ft ramp is 120 in long, so at one inch of rise per twelve inches it suits about a 10 in rise. The VEVOR page states 10 to 20 in, while the CAMMOO, LEMNISCATE and others state 10 to 30 in. At 30 in the slope is far steeper than the rule of thumb, so read the maker's slope guidance and your device manual.

Capacity must exceed the user, the chair or scooter and anything carried. The CAMMOO handrail model lists 1200 lb, the NUWJBYE 850 lb, the VEVOR and CAMMOO folding model 800 lb and the HOMCOM 594 lb. The LEMNISCATE gave no figure in the details we reviewed. A powered chair can weigh several hundred pounds by itself.

A wider deck leaves room for wheels and hands. The CAMMOO 1200 lb and NUWJBYE are 36 in wide, the CAMMOO 800 lb is 29.1 in and the LEMNISCATE 29 in. Raised baffles or side walls act as edge barriers on all six. Check your chair's track width plus clearance.

Rails give a steadying hold for the user and for a helper walking beside the ramp. Only the CAMMOO 1200 lb and NUWJBYE include them, and they add weight and bulk. Rails are not required by every setup, but on a long incline they are worth considering. Rails do not replace supervision.

Grooved or textured aluminum drains water, while carpet grips quietly but holds moisture. The VEVOR lists a grooved surface with a non-slip coating, the CAMMOO lists triple anti-slip, and the HOMCOM uses a frosted skidproof carpet. Wet weather and leaves make any ramp slick, so brush it clean. Reflective strips help in the dark.

A folded ramp has to fit your car or closet. The CAMMOO 800 lb offers two folding options, the LEMNISCATE and others fold to roughly 60 in long, and the handrail models are bulkier. Think about who will lift it, since aluminum 10 ft ramps are heavy. Choose a carry style someone can manage safely.

howWeEvaluated.title: Rise range and slope
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the step heights each page names and worked out the slope on a 10 ft run. The VEVOR is the most conservative at 10 to 20 in, while several rivals state 10 to 30 in. These are maker ranges, and we do not endorse the steep end.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity ratings
howWeEvaluated.description: Listed capacity was compared. The CAMMOO handrail model leads at 1200 lb, the NUWJBYE lists 850 lb, the VEVOR and CAMMOO folding model list 800 lb, and the HOMCOM lists 594 lb. The LEMNISCATE page lacks a figure.

howWeEvaluated.title: Width and rails
howWeEvaluated.description: Deck width and rails were reviewed. The CAMMOO 1200 lb and NUWJBYE are 36 in wide with handrails, while the others are around 29 in without. Side baffles appear across the group.

howWeEvaluated.title: Surface and visibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared grooved aluminum, coatings and carpet, plus reflective strips. The VEVOR and NUWJBYE list reflective strips, and the HOMCOM uses carpet. We did not test grip.

howWeEvaluated.title: Folding and carry
howWeEvaluated.description: Fold options and handles were noted. The CAMMOO 800 lb has two folding options and the LEMNISCATE has a handle. Value reflects what is included, not price.

cards.label: Railed
cards.text: Rails give a hold on a long incline and a wider, fixed deck, at the cost of weight and a larger folded shape. The CAMMOO 1200 lb and NUWJBYE are railed. Choose them for regular use at one door.

cards.label: Bare
cards.text: A folding deck without rails is lighter and stores flat. The VEVOR, CAMMOO 800 lb, LEMNISCATE and HOMCOM are bare, with edge baffles only. Choose them if the ramp travels or is stowed between uses.

howToChoose.note: Rails do not replace help for anyone who needs it, and a helper should still walk alongside on the first few trips until the route feels settled.

faq.q: How long should the ramp be for my step?
faq.a: A common rule of thumb is one inch of rise for every twelve inches of run, so a 10 ft ramp suits roughly a 10 in rise. Longer is gentler. If your rise is bigger, a longer ramp or a different solution may be safer.

faq.q: Is 30 in a safe rise for a 10 ft ramp?
faq.a: Several listings state 10 to 30 in, but a 30 in rise on 120 in is about one to four, much steeper than the rule of thumb. Check your device manual for incline limits and ask a therapist. Many users and helpers will find the upper range unsafe. Pushing a chair up that angle takes real effort, and coming down a steep ramp can run away from a helper. If your rise is near the top of a listed range, ask the seller for the maker's slope guidance in writing and consider a longer ramp.
They give a steadying hold on a long incline, and only the CAMMOO 1200 lb and NUWJBYE include them. They add weight and bulk. Needs vary by user.

Listings describe rain use, but leaves, ice and dirt make any ramp slick. Brush it clean and check the feet and plates. Store it if you can. Before each use, look at the hinges, the pins and the transition plates for bends or play, and make sure the base sits on firm, level ground rather than soft soil or loose gravel. A ramp that moves under a wheel should be taken out of use until it is fixed.

faq.q: Is a portable ramp the same as a permanent ramp?
faq.a: No. A permanent entrance may need landings, handrails and permits, and a portable ramp is not a code-compliant substitute. Check local rules. The ADA slope figure applies to public buildings, not private homes, but many installers use it as a sensible reference. A landing at the top, wide enough for the chair to turn and for the door to open, is often the part buyers forget.

faq.q: Why is the capacity not listed on some pages?
faq.a: Some pages, such as the LEMNISCATE details we reviewed, omit it. Ask the seller before use. Never guess.
An occupational therapist can look at your device, your entry and your helper. They can advise on slope and technique. Bring your measurements.
